core_obligations: Base change the given lifting diagram along R to R' and apply the formal smoothness hypothesis to obtain a dotted arrow from S' to A' (proof lines 9388-9402).
Choose a direct summand decomposition of R' as an R-module, decompose A' accordingly and identify the image of the ideal J' as a direct sum (proof lines 9402-9410).
Show that the complement summand is an ideal in the subring A plus J', and project the composed arrow to A to obtain the required lifting (proof lines 9410-9417).
proof_roadmap: Base change the diagram and lift by hypothesis (proof lines 9388-9402).
Decompose R' and A' along the direct summand (proof lines 9402-9410).
Use that the complement part is an ideal and project to A (proof lines 9410-9418).
difficulty_reason: The lemma descends formal smoothness in the adic topology along a ring map R to R' that embeds R as a direct summand, and the proof is a 31-line argument that follows the definition of formal smoothness literally. It base changes a given lifting diagram along R to R', lifts the dotted arrow by the hypothesis on the base change, decomposes R' as a direct sum of R and a complement, shows that the image of the composed arrow lands in the part of the target where the square-zero ideal is an ideal, and then projects to obtain the required lifting. The two steps with content are the decomposition of the base changed target and the observation that the complement part is an ideal because the square-zero ideal squares to zero.
